notes.title: Development Journal #7 - Erannorth Chronicles has gone Gold ;)
notes.content:
Hi folks!

I'll start with the good news, which is that Erannorth Chronicles has gone Gold and it will release Friday 17 September 2021.

Well, as 'Gold' as it gets. It's not like I'll be making any physical copies, or that I won't be spending the next couple of years fixing bugs. 

But jokes aside. If your hunch is telling you that Gold means wait a couple of months before buying any game, especially a solo dev's project, then you should probably follow your instincts and wait. There will probably be minor bugs, typos and balance issues, but nothing game breaking I hope.

On my end the game is as ready as it can be, and I am really excited to finally share it with all of you.

Release Content


 9 species each with 35 sub-archetypes.
 9 classes each with 48 sub-archetypes.
 2667 cards.
 204 enemies.
 30 locations with 56 challenges & 108 repeatable areas to explore.
 5 Game Modes.


Let's now have a look what's new since the last time we talked!

Perk Preview

One of the most requested QoL during the playtests, was the ability to see the Perks your species and class offers before diving into the game. There is a new perk preview system in place which can let you inspect the Organization, the Species and Class perks individully, or combined, depending which tab you are on.

Here we inspect the Undead perks. In yellow is the unique to Revenant. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/582a720c4f1d2969046424c2976b31b241abff56.jpg

While here we are viewing all our perks, Revenant's, Morheliss' Acolyte's and our organization.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/8d8d8d05ed29afee13177070f429934e092170c7.jpg

Journal

One of my own greatest annoyances was looking around to find Challenges near my level. Since your species can basically land you anywhere in the map and you may not be familiar with that territory.

Your Journal helps you track Challenges close to your level around the map.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/2cdc0535e639310879f42b9b4efb790020d28641.jpg

As you complete challenges, and you gain levels, more entries will show up there and you can plan your journey accordingly. While there I also added a few more challenges in starting areas that were lacking early level content.

New Modes

Gauntlet

As I have probably (over)stated before, Chronicles is all about the sandbox mode, and this where all future development will be heading too. Wait! Who put that Gauntlet mode in there? ːlunar2019madpigː

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/e80faea48e7fc70c73702bbdcd4c6e6135cf9684.jpg

I know that it's something many enjoy over the Sandbox, so that's one reason it got there. The other is that I quite often found myself wanting to just try out a combination before commiting to it. And I think that many will appreciate having that as a vanilla option too.

So this is how Quest mode came to be. It's a quick 3-stage Gauntlet with around 10 nodes each, to check out your starting build and then you can jump in to your favorite sandbox mode with a little more XP under your belt. 

In addition to that it comes with 4 ascensions if you decide that you aren't going to move this character in the sandbox just yet.

Constructed

Well sort of. Having a full constructed mode would be a bit tricky with how the expertise system work. Could easily left you with unplayable decks for example. 

So what the 'Collector' mode does instead, is to give you 36 extra cards on top of your already sizeable collection, bump the copies you can use to 4, and force you to play with a 45 deck in a world where having a Leyline aversion *truly* sucks. So not a mode for everyone, but I think something many people will also enjoy.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/cc0525c92a9d21f29172d51bee9dc02d666baed6.jpg

 Doomsday Clock 

One of the criticism over sandbox is that there is no urgency. And that's actually how many of us like our sandbox. But what if there was a mode where you have 90 days to live. And after that, it's Game Over? I can see some of you grinning while others are making the symbol to ward off evil. 

Well now there is such a mode, which is basically the old Campaign mode plus a new rule. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/ad37a78d83ac24138985e6c146cf794255010454.jpg

Exploration & Conquest are left untouched for the rest of us sandbox purists ;)

Achievements, Cloud Saves, Workshop support etc.

Yes. All that stuff were added too. ;)


So that's all for now folks! 

Next time we'll talk will be at release in a couple of days. 

I do hope you'll enjoy what Chronicles has to offer, as much as I did making it. 

If you have any questions feel free to ask.

notes.title: Erannorth Chronicles Beta Playtest (#3) is now live!
notes.content:
Hi folks!

The beta playtest for Erannorth Chronicles is now live, and will take place from 30 August till 8 September. 

I'd describe the current development status, as quite close to release, but still with typos, a few balance issues and maybe bugs lurking around. Which I hope we'll be catching together.

There is lot of content to try, so have fun! 

Looking forward to hear your thoughts and feedback, and of course if you encounter any glaring issues or bugs. Note, that only 16/9 resolutions are supported in fullscreen mode and I don't think I'll be supporting 16/10, as the whole game layouts need to be redesigned from scratch.

If you participated in the first or second playtest, the same application will update and you can jump right in. Otherwise you can visit the store page for Chronicles and click on the Request Access button.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/557c05b79d6943bc67382eb373db8af5e374c94f.jpg

If you participated in the first playtest you need to start a new game, older characters are probably incompatible and will cause you many unexpected issues and problems.

For a quick overview of what you should expect, you can also check out this video:

[previewyoutube=zDnhS1PIlU0;full][/previewyoutube]

Or read all details in the patch notes below on what changed since Playtest #2.

Beta Playtest (#3) - v0.19.1 - Patch Notes

 New Content 

 Added Conjurer class (Disciple of - Baal, Abalam, Asmodai, Zagan, Vinea & Balam)
 Added Fay species (Seelie & Unseelie).
 Added Shapeshifter species (Werewolf, Werecat, Wererat, Werebat & Werecat).
 Added Celestial species (Angel & Demon).
 Humans can additionally choose the sub-archetype of Nephilim (Half-Angel) or Cambion (Half-Demon).
 Added Knight class (Knight Errant, Commander & Marshal).
 Acolytes can additionally choose the sub-archetype of Morheliss' Acolyte (Necromancer).
 Psychics can now access the Arcana skill through their exclusive Fortune Teller background.
 Added lots of new Cards (There are now 2553 cards in game).
 Added Tutorials.
 Added new Backgrounds, Challenges & Enemies
 Added descriptions in all Challenges.
 Added new Minor locations in the World Map & Points of Interest.


 New Effects & Mechanics 

 Shapeshifting Mechanic 

 RULE CHANGE (from Erannorth Reborn): Shapeshifted characters no longer Discard the non-Primal actions they draw. They can use all their Deck actions normally.
 Shapeshifter PCs assume the form that matches their [Classification] once they use a card with the Shapeshift:1 effect. The matching filename is used to provide the artwork for this transformation. ie. Werewolf.png for the Werewolf etc.
 If a Shapeshifter PC is still in their Hybrid Form as they start they turn (have Shapeshift 1) then they play for free the card named '[Classification] Form' ie. Werewolf Form. (if such a card exists.)


 Fixed Damage 

 FixedDamage:x can be used to define a fixed source of damage matching the cards element. 
 i.e FixedDamage:4, Element:Air, will deal 4 Air damage.
 Fixed Damage doesn't need separate perk modifiers, it will get any benefits 'Damage' has.
 Resistance will apply normally.


 Ripple Effects 

 Whenever [Effect1] triggers create and play a card with [Effect2]. Some examples of Ripple Effect possibilities:
 ie1. Whenever you deal Damage get Defend 2. (RippleEffectDamage:Defend#2)
 ie2. Whenever you gain Defend, discard a card. (RippleEffectDefend:Discard)
 ie3. Whenever you gain Loyalty, Allies heal 2 HP. (RippleEffectLoyalty:HealAllies#2)
 etc.
 All Ripple Effects caused by Card, will trigger together (as individual smart-casted bonus effects) once every other effect in the card resolves.
 You get the bonus effect regardless of Effect1 outcome. i.e Even if the Enemy resists all Damage you'll still get Defend 2 in the first example.
 Notes to Modders: Ripple effects can be given through cards or perks but in both cases are stored as the same QuestState.
 The Syntax differs like so:
 As a Card effect: QuestStateRippleEffect[Effect1]>[Effect2]#[Value]:1 or QuestStateRippleEffect[Effect1]>[Effect2]:1
 ie1. Card Effect: QuestStateRippleEffectDamage>Defend#2:1, is stored as RippleEffectDamage:Defend#2
 As a Perk Reward: QuestStateRippleEffect[Effect1]:[Effect2]#[Value] or QuestStateRippleEffect[Effect1]:[Effect2]
 ie2. Perk Reward: QuestStateRippleEffectDefend:Discard is stored as RippleEffectDefend:Discard
 Each Effect can have a single Ripple Effect associated with it. ie in the part RippleEffectDamage, Damage is a unique identifier but the ripple effect (value of the quest state) can differ.
 ie. If you set RippleEffectDamage:Defend#2 and a bit later RippleEffectDamage:Draw, the second state replaces the first, so whenever you deal damage you'd draw a card.
 If used as a card effect you can have a single Ripple Effect per card. The second Ripple Effect is ignored. Perks can set multiple Ripple effects at once.
 To unset a ripple effect set its value to 'Unset' ie. QuestStateRippleEffectDamage>Unset:1, will remove this Quest State from the player and will disassociate Damage from its ripple effect.
 You can't set a ripple effect as the effect itself, such syntax is ignored because it would otherwise cause an infinite loop.
 ie. QuestStateRippleEffectDamage>Damage:1 or QuestStateRippleEffectDamage>Damage#3:1 is illegal syntax and both effects will be ignored.
 There is a build-in protection against indirect loops. ie. having both these states: Whenever you deal Damage get Defend 2 and Whenever you gain Defend, Deal Damage, will cause the ripple to break. You deal damage, get defend 2, because you got defend you deal damage and the ripple breaks. 
 You can manually make cards to Ignore Ripple Effects by using the BreakRipple:1 keyword.
 Ripple Effect can also be a 'Scripted' effect. 
 ie. Whenever you gain Defend, Heal 3 and Draw 1. (RippleEffectDefend:Healing=3;Draw=1)
 as a Card effect: QuestStateRippleEffectDefend>Healing=3;Draw=1:1
 as a Perk reward: QuestStateRippleEffectDefend:Healing=3;Draw=1
 If used as a card effect there is no card description for the Ripple Effects or the BreakRipple keyword, either can be set as Flavor texts.


 Forsaking Expertises 

 You can choose to Forsake up to 2 Expertises. 
 To Forsake an Expertise click on the down arrow (reduce rank) while its rank is already at 0.
 The expertise text will change to "Forsaken"
 To revert click on the up arrow (increase rank) to set it back to 0.
 Any bonuses granted to that expertise will be lost once you start the game, which can make your Deck unplayable.
 You'll still be able to use * requirement Actions from that Expertise.


 UI Additions/Improvements 

 Expert Mode 

 While in expert mode hovering over cards won't zoom on them, neither show their tooltips.
 You can toggle the expert mode on/off with Shift+X or by clicking on the scroll icon next to the eye. 
 Toggling the expert mode with the shortcut will also hide the currently zoomed card (if any).


 Reveal Intent 

 Shortcut 'I' or the new UI Button can be used to show and update the intent of all Enemies in the battlefield.
 While visible the Intent will update each time you hover over an Enemy, before and after the Enemy Acts and whenever you activate cards making the prediction way more accurate.
 You can press 'I' again to Hide all visible Intents.
 While hidden the Intent will update each time you hover over an Enemy and before and after the Enemy Acts. You can only see it by hovering over the enemy like before.
 This setting will be remembered and persist across sessions.


 Compact View 

 While 'Compact View' is on: 
 Allies will display in 3 columns instead of 2 (6 Allies at once instead of 4), but without their buttons. You can still click to attack & right-click to use their ability.
 Enemies will display in 4 columns instead of 3 (8 Enemies at once instead of 6).
 This setting isn't saved and will only persist for the current session.


 Misc Changes and Additions 

 Merc:1 modifier for Summons was renamed to Elite:1. The relevant rule updated to: If an Elite Summon is already deployed, instead of Summoning a new instance: Reinforce their Lifespan by 50% (of listed stats) & Reactivate them.
 Fae Alliance bonus skills: swapped Herbalism with Nature Magic.
 Ordo Tenebris bonus skills: swapped Occult with Shadow Magic.
 Removed Organization ranks.
 Organizations cards have been assimilated to the various expertises they belong. But you still need the organization to find these cards. 
 Cards that belong in an Organization have the organization's icon in their border.
 If your save file is using an organization, it's recommended to start a new game.
 Organization Perk benefits will apply to all cards.
 When clicking a Skill icon in Attributes & Skills to preview its card set, the card set will load faster & asynchronously (return immediately the first results)
 Clicking the Class/Race badge in Character Sheet will open the Class/Race info in the Rulebook.
 When an Ally use a special that has an ally as its optimal target, they will always try to target themselves first.
 Passive allies will display the text "Passive" instead of a damage range.
 Inactive allies will also become translucent.
 Added an explanation in the early references of LP & PP on what they are used for.
 Tweaked Hirdwood to become suitable as the starting area of the Fay.
 Updated the 'Gameplay basics' section of the Rulebook.
 Changed 'Wildshape' expertise & keyword to 'Shapeshift'.
 Limit:1, can be used in Actions to prevent them from being created if they already exist in player's hand.
 Removed the limit of 4 on how many types an ally can gain through AddAllyType[Type]. They can now gain as many types as your cards allow. (Note to modders: Forcing the change using a value of 5 is no longer necessary.)
 Changed the icon for 'All/Intense' as it was similar to 'Astral' icon
 Improved the clarity of the Element sprites
 In Character sheet: Clicking on the Expertise icon will show its associated cards.
 During character creation the HP displayed there, will also include the Bonus Starting HP from the Game Mode.
 When buying and selling cards in town, the transaction result will also appear directly in the button.
 RULE CHANGE: Invoke & Draw can now draw/create new cards as long as the PC has less than 10 cards in hand (instead of 7).
 Card text will change to reflect how many cards the card will most likely draw. ie. If the card can draw up to 3 cards, and you already have 9, it will show that you can Draw only 1 card. 
 This number will appear in a red color to indicate that it's penalized. 
 This number won't account for any cards that you may discard as a result of playing this card ie. due to Merge, Reaction, Recipe etc. Or if the card has draw conditionals etc. So you may end up drawing more or less.
 Discarding a card will re-evaluate all cards in hand and update any relevant values.
 Changed the visuals of Expert Mode & Cycle Hand to match with the new Reveal button.
 Changed 'Celestial' Magic & Runes to 'Angelic' Magic & Runes.
 Tweaked the Angelic Magic, Angelic Runes & Infernal Magic card sets.
 Tweaked the Leadership card set, Added 'Nobility' expertise/card set.
 Noble Background will now give +1 Nobility (instead of +1 Leadership).
 Changed the Starting Deck and Skill for Hyperion's Acolyte. They can now learn 'Angelic Runes' instead of 'Angelic Magic'.
 Changed how certain effects display. Their declaration is unchanged.
 EnemyBane[Group]:x effect will now display as 'Punish [Group] +x'. ie. EnemyBaneWicked:5, will display as 'Punish Wicked +3'.
 ExpendBuff[Resource]:x effect will now display as 'Pay [Resource] x'. ie. ExpendBuffFarthings:5, will display as 'Pay 5 Farthings'.
 Added a special/shorter notation for "Upgrading" summons (Summons that target a certain Archetype, then Unsummon the old ally and also pay Farthings in order to come in play.)
 In Codex entries: the Appendix section will also include any keywords that are part of a composite/conditional structure.
 Valor Tooltip explanation will change accordingly if the PC has a perk modifying how Valor works.
 Edit several sections of the Rulebook to reflect various rule changes from Reborn to Chronicles. Added a new rulebook section for the World Map.
 In Character Creation the amount of cards in Collection will display next to the button. This number will refresh each time you change something in your character.
 The Perks that change which Ally 'Doom' & 'Contract' summons, will now instead give a (Trinket) card that once played will gives the same benefit. This way you can choose if and when to activate that benefit. ie. Playing 'Morheliss' Gift I' will change your Doom effect to create 'Grave Lurkers'. You don't need to do that again, as this is a permanent change that is saved in your save file. But if later on you get 'Morheliss Gift II', you can use it to change your Doom effect to create 'Plague Zombies'. If you change your mind or need Grave Lurkers, you can replay 'Morheliss' Gift I' to swap back to Grave Lurkers.
 This change won't apply retroactively if you already have taken these perks.
 Athletics is removed for now and its 4 cards moved into a different Expertise.
 Misc Improvements/Optimizations in the Player's Handbook & Enemy Compendium
 Added a 'Kill switch' button in Player's Handbook and Enemy Compendium to manually stop the active search ie. if it's taking a long time or was the wrong search etc.
 Player's Handbook and Enemy Compendium will automatically terminate any active searches, when closed through its x button.
 Player's Handbook and Enemy Compendium will immediately stop loading new results, if the player clicks on a different category before the loading is finished or initiates a different search.
 Added a Banter message, when the Action fails because its requirements weren't met or the player picked the wrong target for this action.
 Added T9 Legendary items require 15+ in their expertise and level 13+ to equip them. They'll appear only as high level area rewards, and you can distinguish them from their (brighter) gold border.
 Added some additional options for opening chests. Lowered slightly the strength reqs for bashing them.
 Increased the cost to maintain Companies.
 Reduced max Ally Power & Health limits. They are set at (180,240) in Exploration & (120,160) in Conquest & Campaign difficulties.
 In Character Creation: the derived panel will include in parenthesis any perk modifiers that can alter the Proficiency or Resistance values.
 After completing an Area added a new Reward Summary
 If completing an area/challenge has rewards like XP, PP, Influence etc. a summary reward screen will appear to display them. 
 This screen won't appear in random encounters as they don't give such rewards.
 Updated the progression section in the rulebook
 In Character sheet implemented part of the Progression tab.
 The first section in the progression tab will display the next level's benefits. New Max HP, New Max AP, New AP / turn, How many HP & AP will get refilled, LP & PP gained.
 Increased World map resolution.
 Added new minor/placeholder locations in the World map. 
 They don't have a special function by default. Minor locations can be tied to a .json location file and used for quests, act as player's homes or starting locations.
 'Areas' in Location.json files can be events. (Trigger events directly in the world map without assigning them to nodes).
 To change the area into an event set "Area_x_CompleteRequirements":"Event::EventID"
 ie. "Area_1_CompleteRequirements": "Event::Headquarters", will start the Headquarters.json event.
 Most other properties of that area can be used to set ie. the cover artwork (Area_1_CoverArtwork), unlock requirements (Area_1_UnlockRequirements), how the activity is named etc.
 ie.

 "Area_1_Name": "Abandoned Camp",
 "Area_1_CoverArtwork": "Abandoned Camp",
 "Area_1_UnlockRequirements": "Level:2",
 "Area_1_CompleteRequirements": "Event::Abandoned Camp",
 "Area_1_isRepeatable": false
 All other area properties are ignored.

 The amount of Completed Challenges is now tracked & saved.
 In Character sheet, Progression tab implemented the progression rewards.
 Progression rewards can be claimed from the Progression tab once certain amount of challenges are completed, or when the player reaches a certain level.
 Clicking a progression reward (similar to perks) will open its codex entry and display any associated cards.
 Notes to Modders: 

 Progression rewards are declared in PerksDB similarly to perks.
 Name must contain the identifier Challenge:: & Level:: if we want these rewards not to also show up in unlocked perks.
 Either CompleteChallenges:x OR ReachedLevel:x must be used to set the reward requirement.
 The rest fields are as you'd expect from Perks.
 The description field is much shorter than in perks, and so the description should much more compact. Excessive text is cut and replaced with ellipsis.

 Added a couple of rewards in progression to test out the system.
 Updated the voice overs of several allies. Thanks @Gaist Heidegger ;)
 Updated the credits section
 Implemented a tutorial system. 
 Added a short tutorial for the various Overworld Map functions/shortcuts. It will display only once after starting a new game.
 A tutorial on Areas and Leylines will appear the first time in the Areas/Activities menu.
 A tutorial on Nodes will appear at the first Dungeon Entry
 A tutorial on using Actions will appear at the first Encounter
 A tutorial/overview of the Character Sheet will appear the first time the Character Sheet opens
 Added a button in Settings to 'Mark all Tutorials as 'Unseen''
 Added Tutorials for the Character Creation sections.
 Challenge names can be used as requirements (as long as they are unique), using Challenge:[Challenge Name] ie. Challenge:Liberate Oggurnvald Keep
 Areas now support a description field. It will display only if "Area_x_Description":"" has a value other than blank.
 [Player Home] You can now liberate the Oggurnvald Keep (The fort below Lanmerih) from the Bandits that live there, and claim it as your Headquarters.
 [New Town Filter] "Don't show me cards I can use 'Untrained'": turning this filter on (and refreshing the merchant) will hide all cards with * Expertise Requirements
 Added codex entry for 'Ripple Effect'
 A banter popup with minimal duration will display whenever a 'Ripple Effect' triggers, as a reminder that something 'extra' happened.
 In Character Creation: After forsaking a skill, a notification will appear under skills to indicate that you can forsake up to 2 skills.
 Tweaked and rebalanced all perks that affect ally Power & Health.
 Tweaked Witch perks and variants
 Tweaked Acolyte Starting Decks
 Added a new Acolyte variant: Morheliss' Acolyte (Necromancer)
 'Dark Witch' bonus expertise changed from Necromancy-oriented to Affliction-oriented (as now there is a dedicated Necromancer variant (Morheliss' Acolyte))
 In World Map:

 Whenever your avatar stands in an area with unique exploration options (major or minor) a prompt will appear in the top panel under the location name: "Press 'M' to Explore".
 Pressing 'M' aside from opening/closing the Area activities will also center the Map to the PC avatar.
 Hovering over a minor location will display a Tooltip with its name. 
 If a minor location has anything worthwhile to do its tooltip will also include a "Point of Interest" tag.
 Clicking on minor locations marked as 'Point of Interest' will open their activities menu to preview what's is there.

 Preview Rewards button will get disabled if the Activity is an Event
 Using Forced March will no longer keep up building up your Fatigue.
 [Point of Interest] Nomad Camp: acts as a small settlement where you can purchase supplies and rest.
 [Point of Interest, Wicked PC home] Mournvale is small village. You can visit the local town (T0). Complete a challenge and finally claim a crypt as your headquarters (if you are Wicked). Mournvale's Mausoleum library upgrade will offer some of the darker expertises as learning options, that are unavailable in other headquarters.
 Added new character Backgrounds. Thanks @Risewild ;)
 Added descriptions in the various Challenges for more RP & immersion.
 Several Challenges are now 'part of a chain'. Completing them unlocks the next part of the chain, which can be another challenge or a treasure hunt and so on.
The following challenges unlock new challenges or events:
 Lanmerih's Arena [Lanmerih] -> Lucina's Arena [Lucina] -> Innford's Arena [Innford] -> Barrow's Bay Pits [Barrow's Bay]
 Igor the Master of Kennels [Geirsver] -> Garmuth Bloodsmasher's Lair [Geirsver] -> Weapon Cache (Geirsver) [Geirsver] -> Ruined War Tower [New Ulnathiir] -> Destroy Varshukh's Loyalists [New Ulnathiir]
 Galdorak War Party [Grysbog] -> Unconventional Remedy [Grysbog]
 Galdorak War Party [Grysbog] -> Galdorak's Rise [Hirdwood] -> Fubakl's Revenge [Hirdwood]
 Galdorak's Lair [Nereis] -> Ascetic Life [Nereis] -> Galdorak's Revenge [Nereis]
 The Missing Fishermen [Herman's Rest] -> Herman's Undercroft [Herman's Rest]-> What Lies Beneath [Herman's Rest]
 Attempt on your Life! [Jarakkal Oasis] -> Speaker of the Eternal [Jarakkal Oasis] -> Cult of the Eternal [Nrekveil]
 Tebitha's Tomb [Nrekveil] -> The Staff of Supreme Power [Nrekveil]
 Trouble in Mournvale's Cemetery [+Wicked] -> Mournvale's Mausoleum
 Emerald Grove Archives [Celaenor] -> Emerald Guardian [Oakstead]
 Path of the Flame [Oakstead] -> Altar of Dominion [Oakstead]
 Liberate Oggurnvald Keep -> Oggurnvald Keep
 Spirit of the Grove [Rivermoor] -> Elixir of Eternal Life [Rivermoor]
 The Broken Council [Roverford Valley] -> The Plot Thickens [Roverford] -> Lord Vannedar [Roverford] -> Master of Shadows [Roverford]
 Skarfjord's Insurrection [Skarfjord] -> Weapon's Cache (Skarfjord) [Skarfjord]
 Unlocked Chain quests (if any) will now display in the Rewards summary screen.
 Once you complete enough challenges to claim a progression reward a reminder message will display in the Rewards summary screen.
 Tweaked/Nerfed Combat V,VI & VII perks.
 Added Starting Locations for Nephilim & Angel characters (Lucina) and for Cambion & Demon characters (Innford).
 In Character Creation: The Starting Deck displayed in Skills & Attributes / Derived wasn't showing up cards that added in Starting Deck with Perks.
 In Save/Load system:

 The summon limit value is now stored in the Save File.
 Perks benefits are calculated before recreating saved allies, as certain perk benefits (like increasing the caps of summon power & heath limit) wouldn't apply correctly on them.
 Added a version control system in save files. Older save files should upgrade automatically (to whatever) the latest save file revision is, once they are loaded.

 Codex entries will now include effects that are part of Gambit or Weave constructs in their Appendix.
 Added a "Special Rules" or "Recommendation" section in the archetypes that need (or should) pick a sub-archetype.
 Added 3x Negotiate cards to Human Starting deck.
 In character creation: If the player tries to start the game with insufficient card collection (fail meeting their min deck requirements) a dialog will show up to notify the player and prevent the game from starting.
 Modding related fixes/tweaks:
 Added a fallback icon for custom archetypes
 Adding custom Expertises via Mods should no longer hide vanilla expertises during Character Creation.
 It's now possible to add a single custom expertise, instead of having to define a list of at least two.
 Added a fallback icon for custom expertises


 Bugfixes 

 Expertise perk bonus for Power, Health & Lifespan wasn't properly displaying on the Card.
 Starting without a Background could cause an exception error.
 Fixed an issue with certain 'Self' Echo Actions not triggering properly.
 Moved the card preview higher. It will be rarer for tooltips to fall over the card itself and ie. block its discard button.
 Fixed a few definition errors in a couple of perks & cards.
 Summon Limit will properly not drop below 0, fixing the 'infinite' summon glitch.
 'For the Pack' is properly excluded from Town Merchants.
 Changed the way bonus HP from the game mode are handled. This should prevent a rare bug that could cause the loss of these bonus HP mid-game.
 Fixed an issue with Merchants not offering the last unowned copy of a Playset.
 The scrollbar position will remain (mostly) unchanged while interacting with the Player's Handbook and Monster Compendium, instead of jumping you to the top.
 Bewitch Damage wasn't refreshing properly the enemy Health bar.
 Alt+Clicking Card Labels while in Character Sheet, was showing their codex entries unformatted.
 Alt+Clicking a Card will no longer show itself as a related card.
 Added a safeguard in Player's Handbook and Enemy Compendium to prevent creating duplicate entries.
 Fixed an exception error that could appear in Enemy Compendium after the introduction of the Enemy Intent Overlay in 0.15.9
 Some of the new ally definitions were missing the miniature keyword and would display as cards instead of characters.
 Eager Conscripts were missing from Commander's starting Deck.
 Slightly reduced the scale of Boss actors to prevent parts of them from getting cut by the scroll area mask.
 Archery Range II was giving only 1 Crossbow Infantry instead of 3.
 Fixed some definition errors in a few ally cards.
 While in Compact view the 'Zzz' status icon of allies is hidden. You can tell if they are active from their transparency.
 While in Compact view, Enemy elements will no longer overlap with each other.
 Exploration event was incorrectly stating that you can Camp through it. You can only camp using the Camp button.
 All Shortcuts are blocked while an Event or Story is running. (including the 'X' shortcut)
 The tooltip on the set preferred target button wasn't always showing up
 While the Compact view was on, newly summoned allies had their buttons visible.
 Fixed NNLB & NNLA card formatting tags to only apply in the card box and not in the codex entry.
 Viewing the Expertise card sets from the Character Sheet could cause the corruption of certain player data for the duration of the session.
 While viewing expertise card sets: Closing the 'view' with cards still loading, will properly stop processing in the background further cards.

notes.title: Development Journal #6
notes.content:
Hi folks!

Playtest #3 is only a few days away, and we already talked a bit (in Development Journal #5) about some of the upcoming features. So let's dive in and see a few more.

 New Player Experience 

(A few) Tutorial texts will now popup at certain places as you play, to guide you on some basic gameplay elements. These tutorial aren't there to replace the Rulebook which is always an F1 key away, but to show you a few basic stuff, you'd probably figure out on your own. Like how to interact with the world map or how to play cards during encounters etc.

These tutorials will only appear once. But if you feel that you need to see them again, there is a button in settings that once clicked it will mark them all as unseen, and they will trigger once more.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/232898bcf8f29a336a8a6dff1ecaa2f3736d990c.jpg

 First Balance Pass 

Balancing 2540 cards and hundreds of archetype combinations in a timely fashion without you is a bit tricky for a solo dev, which I hope we'll be doing it together in Playtest #3. 

But I already went ahead and fixed the most glaring balancing issues I could spot.

 New Acolyte decks and a new Acolyte Variant 

Acolyte variants had a common pool of cards along with these unique to them. Now their whole deck is unique and distinct from each other. There is also a new acolyte variant (Morheliss' Acolyte) which is basically the Necromancer class.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/d787aedc2e599ee2f566ddc8b57637a9dfab2cf7.jpg

Before that a Revenant/Dark Witch could fill this role unsuccessfully, but after this change Dark Witch shifted her focus in curses, hexes and afflictions.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/28999b0d601a3a1c72b82622d45176ff47ca1aea.jpg

 Ripple Effects 

Ripple effects is a new mechanic that basically can associate any card keyword with a bonus effect card. Better explain that with a few examples:

In the screenshot above, the Dark Witch has: 

[Festering Ripple Effect] 
Whenever you play a card with Festering, up to 2 Random Enemies get Bleed 1.

Some notes on Ripple effects.

- Festering can have a single Ripple effect. So if I get another (Festering Ripple Effect) I am essentially replacing this one.
- The bonus effect caused by the Ripple effect triggers after all the card effects resolve. And by resolve I mean that the card didn't fail due to lack of requirements. Festering itself doesn't have to actually have any result.
- Bonus effect values will benefit by Perks or if it's damage your affinities etc. So you can easily end up inflicting more Bleeding down the road.

Let's see another example:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/4af5d8a80256210f6081a777e4b017062f01909a.jpg

The Physician has: [Supplies Ripple Effect]
Whenever you play a card that fetches Supplies, you also get -1 Strain.

The Supplies effect doesn't have to yield any results, but as long as it resolves you get Strain -1.

 Forsaking Expertises 

Each expertise you take can potentially add from a few to hundreds of cards in your card pool that you may not need or feel they aren't exactly suit your RP.

You can click on the 'decrease rank' arrow of an expertise while it has 0 ranks to forsake it.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/99458b0bcbd321313ffc9e23a4fa697abc6bfab1.jpg

Forsaken expertises will be removed from your character even if you have free ranks in them, so be careful not to forsake expertises crucial for your starting deck to work.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/db0a8b26a01728f90a94d03d9c217d6cf208ba61.jpg

To undo Forsaking an expertise revert its rank back to 0, by clicking on the 'increase rank' arrow while the expertise is marked as Forsaken.

 Compact View 

It's quite easy with summoning classes to reach a high summon limit, and lot of allies in the battlefield can translate to lot of scrolling. Compact view changes the ally presentantion from 2x2 to 2x3, and enemy presentation from 2x3 to 2x4.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/f1bf73c307c8db7a5d6413a99593694bc30bf53d.jpg

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/6895a8c7dbf77530ed6d83da4b2d6a24fb349e2f.jpg

So even if you do need to scroll it will merely be a scroll up or down once you hit 7-9 allies. 
Compact view can be toggled on/off using the 'Z' key.

 Minor Location Tooltips 

I got to implement a few of the minor locations in time for playtest #3, so all Minor Location now have a tooltip, to display their name, and also a "Point of Interest" tag if there is something interesting to do there. 

In such cases if you don't mind/need a spoiler, you can click on them  to view what's in there before actually going there, like in the major locations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/3e6c94534c51678e006ba0d4307708961990e3ab.jpg

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/7a6e24c3b12222b6f24341eeb3b6527fa3efb82e.jpg

Challenges Descriptions 

All Challenges now have a different name and a short description to resemble more like quests, give you a little hint on what you'll find there and the vibe if its something that suits your RP to do or not.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/95a8273102d6f5626e959bf5e1872db126c89bb5.jpg

 Mini Questlines (Chains of Challenges) 

It may appear in a first glance that there are less challenges in the world, but there are in fact 25 challenges as we speak, so a few more than in the previous playtest. 

Many of them will appear once you complete a different challenge, forming together mini questlines.

If completing a challenge unlocks a new one, you'll get an extra notification in your Rewards summary.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/0a17c402a4ea3188e871d19dc71ec72396dd8e87.jpg

So that's about it for now. You'll be able to see more stuff once Playtest #3 starts. Will be spamming your news once more at that time to let you know.

If Chronicles sounds something you'd be interested in, make sure to wishlist and follow its Steam page, so you'd be informed first when the (Beta) Playtest #3 starts!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1580800/Erannorth_Chronicles/

That's all folks! See you in September!

notes.title: Development Journal #5
notes.content:
Hi folks!

There are still a few weeks left till September and Chronicles public beta test, so for today, I have you a very juicy news post! We'll be talking about some new features, and since we are getting close(-ish?) to the release version, address the huge elephant in the room: Is Erannorth Chronicles for you? 

So let's just start with that!

What Erannorth Chronicles is not.

Erannorth Chronicles is not a Roguelite Deck Builder. So if you expect something like StS, Monster Train et al, you'll of course be disappointed.

Erannorth Chronicles isn't Erannorth Reborn either, so if you expect an exact clone game, with improved graphics for an 1-1 replacement, high chances are that you'll probably be disappointed too. 

What is Erannorth Chronicles.

Erannorth Chronicles is an Erannorth game. So similarly if you'd expect an entirely different game loop, or a card game that plays itself without reading or learning any of its rules, then you'll probably be disappointed as well.

To borrow the words from one of the best feedback I got: If I should compare Chronicles with Reborn, I don't know why Chronicles are different, It FEELS like pretty much the same old Reborn, but with better graphics and obligatory uninteresting campaign stuff on top of it. 

So let's see.

How Chronicles and Reborn differ anyway?

First difference: Genre. Erannorth Chronicles is a Sandbox RPG/Card Game. While Erannorth Reborn was a Roguelite Card Game with a few RPG Element here and there, and a few modes that would let you play a Sandbox Adventure. Their difference might seem subtle?, but it's all the difference in the world. And can make or break a game for you.

ie. No unlocks can be a really turn off if what you expect is a roguelite game. But also a huge annoyance if you expect an RPG game. In Chronicles, you get the RPG option: you can play anything you want, whenever you want. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/dbd7650b10ac6b2aaf3e1f4f8372479a3896a15e.jpg

So if in doubt, please participate in September's beta and see if it's a game you like. Don't purchase it on day one just because you liked Reborn. 

Because Reborn had aspects Chronicles doesn't. And vice versa. 

And as much hearing it'll be day one purchase from many of you honors me deeply, I'd really hate to see you disappointed guys :)

Which brings us to the second difference: Sandbox Experience. Erannorth Chronicles focus is the Sandbox mode. That's the main (and only mode) I'll be developing for it. Sure Draft, Drifter and other variants for it, but the premise is the same: an obligatory sandbox campaign. 

Sandbox as in no Story, you make your story, no hand to guide your actions, full freedom to go and do whatever you like, be whomever you want to be. etc.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/fe939cf320a70148f4138f50894d10095cda6e3d.jpg

Focusing on Sandbox this time, means two things a) it will (and already has) evolve, way beyond Reborn's Sandbox mode and b) if you never liked Reborn's Sandbox mode, then Chronicles has probably nothing to offer for you. Because Sandbox is what is all about. ;)

Third difference: Character Customization. Erannorth Chronicles offers lots of different Character Customization options Subspecies, Specializations, Backgrounds, Expertises etc. 

While in Reborn you were done in a few seconds in a single screen, here the character creation will take up more screens, more time to decide what to play, way more reading to decide what to play. etc.

As a simple example, the classes and species might seem less than Reborn, because Reborn already had 4 DLCs, UEP and a workshop full of mods, but each of the 9 Species in Chronicles comes with 35 variants and each of the 9 Classes with 47 different specializations. 

While not (always) totally different, they will set you up on a very different path. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/a1118675ccaee774d488f71607e231555684def8.jpg

Chronicles is really heavy on customization, different builds and experimenting. And that's another aspect that some players enjoy while others hate. 

Fourth difference: Development time. Erannorth Reborn had three years of development and 4 DLCs but that's it. Erannorth Chronicles doesn't have any DLCs and it's just getting started. 

And even though they do share the same engine, most of my work went into either adding brand new features, removing stuff that wouldn't fit in or re-inventing cards and archetypes. So in practice, as we speak, Chronicles has about 1/4 of the Development time Reborn has seen. 

To recap: Chronicles is pretty much the same old Reborn, but with better graphics, improved UI, more customization options, an obligatory Sandbox mode on top of it, but most importantly: all my attention and future development plans revolving around it. :)

What's new since last time we talked?

The archetypes have been finalized.

I have finished working on the archetypes and the sub-archetypes for the release version. So aside for some balance passes and tweaks that part is done. As we speak there are about 2541 cards in the game. 9 Species with 35 variants and 9 Classes with 47 different specializations.

If you are curious to know if your favorite archetypes are in, you can skip through this video:

[previewyoutube=bfidVGqjGmY;full][/previewyoutube]

Intent Overlay

One of the most requested features, since Erannorth Reborn, have been the ability to see what the enemies will do exactly. So the new Intent Overlay does just that. There is a button in the UI you can use to turn that on / off. And whenever you play a card with it on, or an enemy acts, their AI response is re-calculated and you can see it, as long as you have encountered & defeated that enemy type before.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/869286cbff52ab33d0bdbc138559aec78c71a162.jpg

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/c316218797ce5da577334b295cf5b37bfdb4acd0.jpg

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/42d58b51093a35c5837ca2088e486d1dcbc2a51b.jpg

 Reward Screen 

Area completion has a new Rewards screen to show you exactly what you got (aside from the cards).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/3fd8c08e01ebafc006213f38310263729016079a.jpg

 Progression 

If you have played in any of the playtests, you may noticed that the 'Skill' cards you used to get every other level in Reborn, are gone. The reason for that, is that cards marked as 'Skills' can't be sold or deleted from your Collection, and in Sandbox you can end up with pretty huge card collections. Not being able to sell or remove cards would have been problematic.

Instead you get the Progression tab, which will have some free perks you can pick once you reach a certain level or complete a certain amount of challenges. It will also show you the exact benefits you'll earn in the next level (HP, AP, AP/turn etc.)

The content in the following progression tab is still work in progress. But you get the point ;)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/d05c1cdaadad3507571379bff7b48705a814642b.jpg

 So what are you working on now? 

As we are heading towards the beta release, my focus has shifted from character customization, on the world map itself, adding new events and also implementing support for minor locations.

 Minor locations? 

Glad you asked! Here for example my character is in such a minor location called Darkthorne Abbey.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/fac6908b03cb3cc283c541eef1c6eb15076e0c51.jpg

There isn't anything special to do there in the build I have. But such minor locations are now fully moddable, ie. can have their own location files. and a modder could go and hook there 20 new areas to explore, or challenges, or quests, or maybe a player base/home? Similar to what they can do in any major location. They can also act as starting locations for the player. 

Hmm what's with this little Island...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/b5a28f7a2dc2d426f28074d22b6cc514e9c44a04.jpg

Indeed there are 5 different landmarks in that island that could host adventures, and areas to explore!

There are actually over 20 such (minor) landmarks as we speak, that is aside major locations like Lanmerih etc. But the actual extend in which these areas will be utilized (on release) is still unknown. 

There are way too many challenges and places to explore already and too much content that if I keep adding more and more the game will simply never see the light out of my basement. For now take it as something I made for modders to use.

But you did ask what I am working on now, so... there you have it. :P

 Closing comments 

Phew, that was too long of a post. But I think it covers most major additions since Playtest #2. 

I'll now be going off the radar till September, to do some world building. ;)

If Chronicles sounds something you'd be interested in, make sure to wishlist and follow its Steam page, so you'd be informed first when the Beta Playtest starts!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1580800/Erannorth_Chronicles/

That's all folks! See you in September!

notes.title: Erannorth Chronicles Alpha Playtest (#2) is now live!
notes.content:
Hi folks!

The second alpha playtest for Erannorth Chronicles is now live, and will take place from 25 July till 06 August. After that we'll be meeting again in September - hopefully with the beta playtest. ;)

I'd describe the current status, as 'still alpha, but things start slowly to shape up'. 

There is lot of content to try, so have fun! 

Looking forward to hear your thoughts and feedback, and of course if you encounter any glaring issues or bugs. Note, that only 16/9 resolutions are supported in fullscreen mode.

If you participated in the first playtest, the same application will update and you can jump right in. Otherwise you can visit the store page for Chronicles and click on the Request Access button.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40271242/557c05b79d6943bc67382eb373db8af5e374c94f.jpg

If you participated in the first playtest it is highly recommended to start a new game, otherwise you'll experience all sort of bugs and inconsistencies.

For a quick overview of what you should expect, you can also check out this video:

[previewyoutube=3cE456LXi88;full][/previewyoutube]

You can read more details in the patch notes below.

Alpha Playtest #2 - v0.15.0 - Patch Notes

 New content 

 Psychic class is playable. Available archetypes are: Spiritualist, Telekinetic, Telepath & Charlatan.
 Dwarf species is playable. Available archetypes are: River Dwarf, Mountain Dwarf, Runecaster & Bloodsworn.
 Nymph species is playable. Available archetypes are: Dryad, Orestiad, Lampad, Aurai & Nereid.
 Humans can now choose the 'Nomad' classification.
 Naga species is playable. Available archetypes are: Marsh Naga, Frost Naga & Desert Naga.
 Undead species is playable. Available archetypes are: Vampire, Revenant & Wraith.
 Added character backgrounds.
 Added new cards, equipment and perks.
 Added new Enemies, Bosses & Challenges.
 Added new Player Portraits.
 Added some extra Starting gear options.


 Misc Improvements & QoL Additions 

 Added a button in enemies to mark them as your 'preferred' target. Right-Click and any automatic actions (i.e bonus effects, equipment) etc. that can target them, will do so instead of targeting the first enemy. If no enemy is set as 'preferred' then the first enemy is used instead.
 Combat Log window can move freely around. To move it, click and hold the log's four-pointed arrow and move it around with the mouse.
 The Combat Log has four new buttons: 'Small', 'Medium' and 'Large' buttons will adjust the Log's size, while 'Reset' (or shortcut R) will return it back to its original size and position.
 In Character Creation: Starting Deck cards from the base species & class are now also hyperlinked.
 You can now sell your Consumables (and Trinkets) in Towns. In the case of Consumables, each use you have consumed reduces the item's value.
 Added a - button under the Background, Organization & Starting Kit options to clear them out quickly.
 During Character Creation: Perk bonus/penalty modifiers for Summon Limit, AP, HP, Min Deck & Handsize will now show up in the Attributes section.
 Added a new button next to the 'Hand' area, which can be used to cycle between three different Hand views.  a) The default view, is what was already there. b) The full view, will move the hand up to display the full cards. c) The compact view, will move the hand even more down and will switch all cards to full artwork mode. (The shortcut H can also be used to cycle through these views as well.)


 Bugfixes 

 Fixed several typos. Fixed some typos/definition mistakes in a couple of Perks.
 Oakwood West area was missing its picture.
 Dungeon sub-Areas were referencing Factions that don't exist causing some rooms to appear empty.
 Synergy effects weren't receiving their proper modifiers from Expertise-based perks. i.e Strain.
 Book of Heroes characters were missing the portrait artworks.
 While loading the last played preset any subspecies or specializations that doesn't match that will be cleared out.
 Presets should now properly store the assigned expertise ranks along with attributes.
 Imps & Fiends will properly count as Wicked.
 Right-Click while hovering over a card with an active arrow will just cancel the Arrow instead of casting it.
 Fixed an issue with resistance/affinities appearing double if the setting "Show Enemy Resistances as Text" was checked.
 In Character Sheet: The tooltip predicting the AP gain when Willpower or Agility is increased wasn't taking into account that for this calculation Willpower & Agility penalty can't drop the player's AP below their Base AP.
 The defend sprite that was used in some ally abilities wasn't matching the defend icon in PC statuses.
 ReCloning a card with the console will no longer cause it to lose its element.
 Bone Altar's Necromancy choice wasn't giving any Undead Minions.
 Some contact cards weren't properly excluded from the random loot tables.
 Buy/Sell buttons of the last row of Commodities in Town Card view were outside the viewport.
 Looting interface was showing the wrong amount of picks left if the allowed picks were 3 or more.
 Backpack card count was inaccurate in certain cases.
 The encounter notification, event & exploration options in the world map will properly block further movement while active.
 Targeting arrow will no longer popup right after targeting an ally with a card.
 Fixed an exception error that could be caused by the ally arrow targeting an enemy.
 The target arrow would some times raycast the table (and smart cast the action) instead of the intended/targeted ally.
 Tweaked the enemy area as enemies with enlarged graphics (ie. bosses), were getting cut in certain spots.
 Set as preferred target button was blocked for the second row enemies.
 Tweaked the initial placement of the PC token, as in some cases was outside of the town borders.
 When Camp was breaking due to Encounter, the Encounter popup was displaying the wrong info about hours passed, ap & hp restored etc.
 Overworld AP & HP display wasn't refreshing in certain cases ie. after gathering wood.
 Fixed an issue with the description of the Psychic/Charlatan combination turning all into a hyperlink.
 Fixed a part of the North Coast sea mesh near Rivermoor that was overlapping the coast and was switching the avatar to sea voyage while in land.
 Loitering in town wasn't updating visually the time-stamp.
 Fixed an issue with Map movement getting blocked if allies are in play.
 The padlock indicator (that you can't use a card), should now only appear in cards if they are in the player's hand.
 Gather Herbs activity in Explore & Camp options wasn't checking for the AP requirement.
 During character creation: Info panel's title wasn't refreshing after picking a background.
 'Tarot Deck' card was getting added at Inventory instead of Stash.
 After character creation, additional AP or HP increases from perk bonuses were only applying only to the Max HP/AP, giving the weird feeling that you started the game wounded. The only case that you can start the game with less than max HP is if you have a background perk that sets your HP to a certain value.
 Retirement dialog had black text on gray backround.
 The active synergy text could overlap with the full art card name and the enemy healthbar, while the hand zone was at full card view. 
 Added a check when starting a new game to ensure that the previously chosen archetype/sub archetype pairings are still valid.
 Towns will now properly show allies that are part of the local population


 Content Updates 

 Slightly nerfed & also reduced the tiers of Fury actions. Their expertise requirements are unchanged.
 Edited/tweaked several card sets. (Infernal Magic, Affliction, Necromancy, Rituals, Blood Magic & Runecasting)
 Acolyte main skill changed from 'Lore' to 'Unarmed'
 Adjusted the early level areas of several locations to allow starting the adventure there.
 Removed the 'no-ration' rest option from the camping menu.
 Camping is allowed in locations where you are denied entry to the town.
 Added Untrained options for gathering fruits and hunting. Gathering fruits is easier (except for the rare ocassion of food poisoning). Hunting is a bit harder but better than starve in the wilderness.
 Reduced the initial Summon limits of many species and classes to 2 or 1. Certain specializations and classifications can boost this initial limit by +1 or +2.
 Edited/tweaked several card sets. (Fae Alliance, Canticum Noctem & Resurgant Tenebris).
 Removed the old affiliation data from the various map locations as they weren't currently in use. (Locked Towns are still locked and get unlocked once the influence modifier reaches +2).
 'Gather Wood' choice won't appear in Camp/Explore options if the player already has 10 (or more) Wood.
 Tweaked Ulniir archetypes.
 Added a couple more Dhampir-specific perks.
 Changed the starting location of some archetypes: Elosians will now start in Lucina, Dhampirs in Innford, Centaurs & Satyrs in Rivermoor.
 Tweaked the difficulty settings for Conquest & Campaign.
 If a card has an alternative effect that triggers by discarding it, and also has an expertise requirement, then you'll need to have at least that much expertise to use that discard effect.
 Added demographic information (for the currently implemented species) in the world locations
 Updated Imports/Exports information in the world locations.
 Locked towns will now display the influence at which they'll unlock (175).
 Assigned the enemies groups to different environments.
 Replaced the 'Tutorial' difficulty with 'Exploration' difficulty. It's still extremely easy but mechanically similar to the harder modes. ie. There are ambushes but with a very low chance, leylines are very weak but are there, scaling happens at a lower rate etc.
 'non-Undead' target should be defined (and is displayed) as 'Living'. All card texts and Perks changed to reflect that. Allies and Enemies that count as living get this tag in their type.


 Rule Changes 

Main & Offhand items are now drawn *after* the Draw step along with the rest 'Active' equipment. Before: Hand size 4 + Main + Offhand would equal a hand of 4 cards (Main, Offhand & 2 Deck cards). Now: Hand size 4 + Main + Offhand equals a hand of 6 cards (4 Deck cards, Main, Offhand).

 Dual Wield 

Many weapons are now designated as Dual Wield and can be used in either slot.

 Clicking the + Icon equips the weapon in the Main slot and changes the button to 'M' to indicate that the weapon is equipped as Main.
 Clicking the 'M' Icon equips the weapon in the Offhand slot and changes the button to 'O' to indicate that the weapon is equipped as Offhand.
 Clicking the 'O' Icon equips the weapon in the Main slot and changes the button to 'M' to indicate that the weapon is equipped as Main again.
 You can unequip and swap dual wield weapons normally.


 Forced March 

In Camp menu you can activate 'Forced March' instead of resting. 

 For Wraith & Revenant characters Forced March works like this:
  You travel in your real form.
  You don't require rest or sustenance but retain the fatigue status.
  Very high % for encounters per hour traveled. ([2% + hour traveled] instead of 2%)
  For everyone else it works like this:
  You lose 2 HP and 1 AP every hour you travel in Forced March.
  Increased % for encounters per hour traveled ([2% + hour traveled / 2] instead of 2%)
  Fatigue will keep accumulating, so after a forced march you'll need more time to get back to normal.
  Forced March is disabled automatically when you rest. 
  Forced March is also disabled if your HP run too low (below 5) or trigger an Encounter.


 Other changes 

 In Enemy Gallery/Enemy Details: The backdrop enemies appear will randomly change.
 In Character Sheet: AP & HP will display as 'Current/Max' instead of 'Current'
 Changed Blood Surge status icon. Blood Surge will now display as an Icon in cards.
 If the card preview in Character sheet stays open for any reason, hovering over it will hide it.
 Allies spreaded out a bit because the plague zombies were too smelly. The ally zone will now show 4 Allies at a time before the scrollbar appears.
 PC avatar in map will now look towards the direction its moving.
 Optimized the algorithm handling World Map locations
 Activities menu in locations now supports scrolling
 Activity type will display as icon.
 Adjusted a bit some of the sub-species descriptions to give them more flavor.
 Tweaked the presentation of the demographic information.
 Enemies in Enemy Compendium are now sorted by their 'Power'.
 Removed references of tokens & mastery from score screen. Added level reached & days passed.
 Small & medium tooltips will auto-adjust themselves to stay inside the screen
 Personal Details will now display the Player's starting Wealth & Rations, including any perk bonus or penalties.


 Modding Additions 

 New Perk Rewards: ModifyEffectMerchantDiscount:x, can be used to give the player x% discount when buying stuff from merchants (down to 10 farthings) and x% more profit when selling stuff to merchants.
 In Events: CardCount:[Cardname][=][value] can be used to check if the player owns a certain amount of cards. ie. CardCount:Wood Drop:[Cardname], DropChance:[Chance]
  ie. Drop:Field Dressing, DropChance:25 (once the enemy dies, there is a 25% chance to give us a 'Field Dressing' card in our hand.
 Note to modders: The PC doesn't loot this card, they just get a temporary copy into their hands. If we want the player to loot this card, ie. it's a weapon or a potion etc. we can either use a container card like a Knapsack or something, or use the 'DeathEvent' trigger instead and hook a looting event on the Enemy's death.
 You can allow this drop only if the PC also has at least a rank in a certain Expertise using additionally DropIfExpert:[Expertise]
 ie. Drop:Field Dressing, DropChance:25, DropIfExpert:Hunting, the card will drop only if we have Hunting.
 You can allow this drop only if the PC also has over a certain rank in a certain Expertise using instead DropIfExpert:[Expertise]#[Rank]
 ie. Drop:Sturdy Chest, DropChance:25, DropIfExpert:Thievery#3, the card will drop only if we have Thievery 3+.
 In game examples: Wolf and Boar variants have a 25% to drop the 'Field Dressing' card, if the PC has Hunting 1+. The two Mimic variants have a 25% to drop a 'Strongbox' (or a 'Sturdy Chest'), if the PC has Thievery 1+ (or Thievery 3+). More will be coming.
